changelog:
AEGIS (v8.0.1) - Hotfix: the Control Room APPLY button was inert.
- [FIX] APPLY_CONFIGURATION in THE CONTROL ROOM did nothing. The modal form wrapped two further forms belonging to THE ESCAPE POD, and a form element cannot be nested inside another form: the HTML parser drops the inner start tag, so its end tag closed the OUTER form in the middle of the Escape Pod card. Everything below that point - the Telegram settings, the passcode field and the APPLY button itself - ended up outside the form, so a submit button with no form owner is simply inert and the save handler never fired. The Escape Pod buttons now target standalone forms of their own through the HTML5 form="" attribute, and the APPLY button is back inside the Control Room form.
- [FIX] The same defect silently hijacked both Escape Pod buttons. EXPORT CORE DATABASE sat inside the Control Room form, so clicking it ran a settings save instead of exporting the database, and BACKUP WHOLE STATION bubbled its submit into the same handler. Both now submit their own forms only.
- [FIX] The save handler relabelled the wrong button while saving: it located the Apply button with querySelector('button[type=submit]'), which resolves to the first submit button in the form's DOM subtree - now an Escape Pod button. It targets the Apply button by id instead.
- [VERIFIED] Reproduced the original defect in a browser against the v8.0 markup (APPLY had no form owner at all), then verified the fix end to end on a throwaway instance: toggling THE LIGHTHOUSE PROTOCOL and pressing APPLY persists lighthouse_opt, station_name and station_bio, and the station's registration payload is built and transmitted.
- [NOTE] Includes the entire v8.0 security and architecture overhaul: the unauthenticated transmitter endpoint, the OTA remote-code-execution chain, CSRF and POST-only enforcement, SSRF guards with TLS verification, and the restored brute-force lockout. Operators still on 7.x or earlier should read RELEASE_NOTES_v8.0.md as well.
